To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
native and recombinantly produced Cry1Ba protein are toxic to L. cuprina larvae in vitro but are not effective in preventing fly strike on sheep.
native and recombinantly produced Cry1B protein is toxic to blowflies and that the native protein is effective in preventing experimentally induced flystrike in sheep.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an environmentally benign, safe, and effective alternative to chemical control of sheep fly strike.
the development of a novel biological control method for the treatment of fly strike in sheep.
the potential use of native Bt and recombinant Bt to protect sheep from flystrike, and the results suggest that native Bt is a more promising approach than is the use of recombinant B. thuringiensis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bt strains that produce Cry1Ba have some potential for preventing fly strike, but that the efficacy of these Bt strains is variable and unpredictable.

Bt is not suitable for use as a preventative measure against fly strike.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bt spore/crystalline preparation provided some protection from fly strike, but that the protection was short lived.
the use of Bt as an alternative to chemical fly strike control in sheep is feasible, although the efficacy is not yet satisfactory.

Bt spore/crystalliferous preparations containing Cry1Ba were effective in preventing experimentally induced fly strikes in sheep for periods of time that were related to spore/crystals being present in sufficient numbers on the fleece.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cry1Ba-producing Bt is toxic to L. cuprina larvae and has potential to prevent experimentally and naturally acquired ovicidal fly strike.
Bt strains expressing Cry1Ba can provide protection against fly strike in sheep, but that the level of protection is not as high as that provided by a commercially available insecticide dip.
